text:
alice.support: incoming ticket from Acme (ticket #AC-4578) — users report intermittent failures when signing in via GitHub SSO. Error shown in-app: \"state_mismatch\" on redirect to /auth/callback. Customer says it succeeds from home networks but fails on corporate network behind a perimeter appliance. Attached they included a stacktrace and a short HAR.

sam.eng: can you paste the full callback URL we saw in the HAR (including querystring)? need to confirm if state or redirect_uri were mutated. also any request ids from our auth service logs would help.

alice.support: paste from HAR (redacted client_id):
```
GET /auth/callback?code=gho_ABC123&state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...%2B%2F...%3D HTTP/1.1
Host: app.redwood.example.com
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 16_1 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Mobile/15E148
Referer: https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=...
```
Note: the state value in HER is long (~1200 chars) and contains plus signs and slashes that are URL-encoded. Customer also attached our auth service log showing a 400 with reason PKCE_VERIFIER_MISMATCH and our correlation id: cor-id=ryu-9f2b.

julie.platform: interesting — the corporate appliance (we know from their ticket) rewrites some headers and performs URL canonicalization. My first suspicion is double-encoding or a change in percent-encoding semantics during the redirect chain. Are they using any intermediate proxy that may convert %2B to + or strip padding?

sam.eng: i pulled our auth-proxy logs around cor-id=ryu-9f2b:
```
2026-03-12T14:23:11Z auth-proxy[instance-3] INFO incoming GET /auth/callback?code=gho_ABC123&state=eyJ...%252B%252F...%253D host=app.redwood.example.com forwarded-for=10.2.0.45 x-forwarded-proto=https x-forwarded-port=80
2026-03-12T14:23:11Z auth-service[main] WARN pkce: verifier length mismatch expected=86 got=60 cor-id=ryu-9f2b
```
Note the proxy shows the state value with %25 sequences (i.e., it received an already-encoded payload). Also x-forwarded-port=80 paired with proto=https — suspicious.

alice.support: customer says their corporate appliance performs SSL inspection and re-terminates TLS, then forwards to our load balancer. They also run URL normalization rules. Could that explain the %25 double-encoding?

sam.eng: yes — if the appliance re-encodes already-encoded querystrings or collapses %2B into +, that will change the exact bytes of the state string and thus change the pkce verifier when we compare. PKCE verifier check is on the code exchange, but if the state roundtrip isn't identical we treat it as mismatch. The unexpected x-forwarded-port might also cause our callback matcher to reconstruct redirect_uri differently when validating the token exchange (we canonicalize host+port).

julie.platform: repro steps to simulate their chain: 1) GitHub redirects to our /auth/callback with encoded state. 2) corporate proxy decodes then re-encodes querystring. 3) our auth-proxy receives a double-encoded state. Sam, can you try curl simulating that?

sam.eng: tried this locally to simulate double-encoding and port mismatch:
```
# original redirect (what GitHub sends)
curl -v "https://app.redwood.example.com/auth/callback?code=gho_ABC123&state=eyJabc%2Bdef%2Fghi%3D"
# proxy re-encodes to %25 sequences
curl -v "http://app.redwood.example.com/auth/callback?code=gho_ABC123&state=eyJabc%252Bdef%252Fghi%253D" -H "X-Forwarded-Proto: https" -H "X-Forwarded-Port: 80"
```
Result: in the second case our service treats the state as different and the exchange fails with the same PKCE_VERIFIER_MISMATCH.

alice.support: customer asked if there is a short-term workaround while they engage their network team.

sam.eng: short-term options: - relax strict equality check for state? risky. - support alternate state passing (use a short one stored in a SameSite=strict cookie before redirect, validate on return). We already accept cookie-based CSRF for some legacy flows; we could enable that for this flow as a toggle per-tenant. For now, recommended: ask the customer to configure the appliance to avoid re-encoding querystrings (typically an option in the rewrite rules) or to forward the original encoded bytes.

julie.platform: ops note — there was an unrelated auth-proxy config push two days ago that changed how we log / normalize querystrings for analytics, but it shouldn't alter payloads. roll logs show:
```
2026-03-10T03:12:01Z deploy-bot: rolled auth-proxy v2.14.1 -> v2.14.2 (config: query-normalize=true)
```
I don't think that toggle modifies the bytes we forward, just how we index them. still, i'll enable extra debug capture for incoming callbacks for the affected tenant (Acme) to confirm.

deploy-bot: debug-capture enabled for tenant=acme corp, window=30m.

alice.support: communicated repro and short-term guidance to Acme. they will try toggling the appliance rule and report back. i'll leave this thread open and post the capture output once julie has it. :thumbsup:

acme.bob: thanks — our network team will try to disable "URL-normalize" rule and test. will follow up by EOD PST.

sam.eng: follow-up action items: 1) julie to paste capture for cor-id if captured. 2) if confirmed double-encoding, we will implement per-tenant cookie fallback in auth flow (low-risk feature flag) — sam to spike. 3) support to keep customer updated.

julie.platform: noted. if we get a cor-id showing %25 in the query, we'll attach it here.

alice.support: thanks team. keeping ticket open.
